methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a Seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen that has raised $9.3M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises six private transportation companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and EarthGrid; no public comparables exist in a sufficiently narrow peer cohort.

Valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression methodology, as peer-median triangulation is not applicable. The transportation sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables (fewer than three datapoints in each narrow filter) to support a robust peer multiple approach. The stage-progression method uses the $9.3M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $23M. This represents a conservative assumption about typical capital-efficiency progression in frontier transportation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M to $27M, with a median of $23M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include the nascent state of the peer set (limited comparable transaction data), execution risk inherent to Seed-stage frontier-tech ventures, and sensitivity to the assumed step-up multiplier. A more robust triangulation would require additional precedent transactions or clearer financial metrics (revenue, unit economics) to validate the progression assumption.
